**2. ثُمَّ لَمْ يَرْتَابُوا۟ — "and afterward doubt not."** Ibn Kathir: they do not have doubts and their faith was not shaken; rather their faith remained on conviction. The word "afterward" stretches the claim across time. It is not enough that belief was true at the moment of entry; it has to survive what comes after — which is precisely what was missing in the Bedouins, in whose hearts faith had not yet entered and settled.

**3. وَجَٰهَدُوا۟ بِأَمْوَٰلِهِمْ وَأَنفُسِهِمْ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ — they strove with their wealth and their lives for the cause of Allah.** Ibn Kathir: they **gladly** gave away their life and the most precious of their wealth in obedience to Allah, as a means of seeking His pleasure. Wealth is named before life — and note the contrast with Banu Asad, who came to Madinah to *take* from the ṣadaqat funds. The true believer is identified by what he gives, not by what he collects.

**أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلصَّٰدِقُونَ** — *those are the truthful.* Ibn Kathir catches the sting: truthful **in their statement, if they say that they are believers** — unlike some Bedouins, who are faithful only by words outwardly. The whole passage began with a *claim*; ayah 15 tells you who is entitled to make it.

## Ayah 16: "Will you inform Allah of your religion?"

**قُلْ أَتُعَلِّمُونَ ٱللَّهَ بِدِينِكُمْ** — *Say: will you inform Allah of your religion?* Ibn Kathir puts the rebuke plainly: *will you inform Allah of what is in your hearts?* To announce your faith as a credential is, without meaning to, to behave as though Allah needed telling.

Then the answer: **وَٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ** — *while Allah knows all that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth.* Ibn Kathir: nothing in the heavens and earth, **even the weight of a speck of dust**, nor anything bigger or smaller, ever escapes His observation. **وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمٌ** — *and Allah is All-Aware of everything.*

The logic is quietly devastating. The one thing your listeners cannot verify — the state of your heart — is the one thing already fully known to the One whose verdict decides everything.

## Ayah 17: who is doing whom a favour

**يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ أَسْلَمُوا۟** — *they regard as a favour to you that they have embraced Islam.* Ibn Kathir identifies exactly what they meant: they considered embracing Islam, and following and supporting the Messenger ﷺ, as **a favour to him**. Allah refuted their false statement: **قُل لَّا تَمُنُّوا۟ عَلَىَّ إِسْلَٰمَكُم** — *Say: do not count your Islam as a favour to me* — because, in Ibn Kathir's words, **the benefit of your Islam will only be yours, and this is a favour from Allah to you.**

**بَلِ ٱللَّهُ يَمُنُّ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْ هَدَىٰكُمْ لِلْإِيمَٰنِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ** — *nay, but Allah has conferred a favour upon you that He has guided you to the faith, if you indeed are true* — true, Ibn Kathir says, **in your claim that you are believers.** The whole account is reversed: the debt runs the other way, and always did.

Ibn Kathir sets against this a scene from the day of the battle of Hunayn, where the Prophet ﷺ addressed the Ansar: *"O Ansar! Have I not found you astray and Allah guided you through me? Were you not divided and Allah united you around me? Were you not poor and Allah gave you riches through me?"* And whenever he ﷺ asked them any of these questions, they would reply: **"Allah and His Messenger have most favoured us."**

Two groups, one situation. Banu Asad arrive in drought and poverty and say, *you owe us*. The Ansar, who gave their city and their wealth and had every human ground to feel owed, answer: *the favour is Allah's and His Messenger's upon us.* That is what a heart looks like once faith has actually entered it.

Maʿārif ul Qurʼān draws the same lesson as a rule for anyone: true and sincere faith is the most precious possession of a Muslim; by accepting Islam a person shows no favour to anybody — on the contrary, it is a favour of Allah that he is guided to the Truth.

## Ayah 18: the seal of the surah

**إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱللَّهُ بَصِيرٌۢ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ** — *Verily, Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is the All-Seer of what you do.* Ibn Kathir: here Allah reminds us that He has **complete knowledge of all creation and that He sees them all.**

Two divine attributes close the surah, and between them they cover the two halves of a human being. His knowledge of the **ghayb**, the unseen, covers the hidden — the intention behind the claim, the faith that has or has not entered the heart. His being **Baṣīr**, All-Seeing *of what you do*, covers the visible — the deeds, including fouled streets and inflated prices. Nothing inward is unknown to Him; nothing outward is unwitnessed.

Ibn Kathir ends his commentary on the surah exactly where a believer should end this passage: *"all praise is due to Allah, all the favours are from Him, and from Him comes the success and protection from error."*

## Living it

**Say the true, smaller thing.** The Qur'an did not tell these men to stop speaking — it told them which word they had actually earned. There is safety in describing yourself modestly: *I am a Muslim; I am trying to obey.* Claiming a higher grade than the one you have earned is the very move corrected here, and it echoes the surah's earlier point that it is improper for any man to claim self-sanctification.

**Faith is measured by what survives, and by what it costs.** Ayah 15 gives the test in two parts: no doubt afterwards, and striving with wealth and life for the cause of Allah.

**Never present your religion as a favour to anyone.** Not to Allah, not to His Messenger ﷺ, not to a community, a masjid or a family. Ayah 17 forecloses it: the benefit is yours, and the guidance was a gift. The correct posture is the Ansar's answer at Hunayn.

**Do not despair at the diagnosis.** The men in ayah 14 were told that faith had not yet entered their hearts — and in the same breath, that obedience would cost them nothing in reward and that Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful for those who repent and return to Him. "Not yet" is not "never." Obey, and let the faith arrive.
